description: Nonempty text does not show that T was written. In the check, c reads the synthetic T and then F through #, so the text of tt is "f", tt has ~written, and c is a second reading. The engine is right here, and a grammar that means "T was written" observes the token, as reparse-written-observation-head does (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a A [+T] f
%rule b A [+T] [+T] f
%rule c A $t(tt)
%conditions ~written ⊆ tags($t)
%rule tt [+T #] <text($) ≠ "" ⟹ ~written>
%rule # [{F}]
%rule f F
